title: Steam Deck performance gets a reality check with Valve's new FPS data
gist: Valve has begun publishing anonymized, opt-in Steam Deck frame-rate averages and histograms on Steam Store pages, exposing wide performance gaps among 'Verified' games and showing many 'Unsupported' titles run well. Hidden client strings hint at a broader PC 'Framerate Estimator'.

insights.claim: Valve now shows anonymized opt-in frame rate averages and histograms for Steam Deck and Steam Deck OLED on many Steam Store pages, using data collected since February.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: Valve's platform telemetry gives it a data moat over third-party performance sites and strengthens Steam as a storefront.
insights.locator: Valve has been collecting anonymized frame rate data

insights.claim: Valve says its Steam Deck frame rate data consolidates around narrow ranges despite biases from VSync, frame-rate caps and custom in-game settings.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: Fixed hardware makes crowd-sourced performance data reliable — an advantage of console-like PC devices.
insights.quote: found that the framerate data consolidates around relatively narrow ranges.
insights.locator: Valve acknowledges that players enabling VSync

insights.claim: Steam Deck 'Verified' status masks wide performance differences: Cyberpunk 2077 averages 30-40 FPS on the Deck while Skyrim: Special Edition usually reaches 50-60 FPS, despite identical badges.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: Binary compatibility badges understate quality variance; granular data could shift purchase behavior on handheld PCs.

insights.claim: Several games Valve labels 'Unsupported' on Steam Deck, including Starfield, Silent Hill 2 and Assassin’s Creed Syndicate, show highly playable user-reported frame rates, with Syndicate near 60 FPS on Steam Deck OLED.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: Real-world data may unlock sales of titles previously deterred by 'Unsupported' labels.
insights.locator: Valve's frame rate data is even more useful for games

insights.claim: Anti-cheat incompatibility makes games like Watch Dogs 2 officially Unsupported on Steam Deck, yet users report 40+ FPS in single-player, showing frame data can separate multiplayer blockers from playability.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: Anti-cheat remains the main structural barrier for SteamOS adoption in multiplayer gaming.
insights.locator: Frame rate data can also be useful for judging the single-player modes

insights.claim: Strings found in Steam client JSON files in April point to a possible Steam 'Framerate Estimator' that would chart estimated frame rates for a chosen app and PC configuration based on other users' data.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: Such a tool would displace third-party FPS estimator sites and could influence PC hardware upgrade decisions.
insights.locator: Back in April, JSON files buried in the Steam client
